tr.td: Non-contrast low-dose CT of the abdomen and pelvis: single 2.6 cm bladder stone of about 420 Hounsfield units, suggesting uric acid; no kidney or ureteric stones; no hydronephrosis; enlarged prostate
12-lead electrocardiogram: sinus rhythm, no left ventricular hypertrophy
Uroflowmetry: maximum flow 8.5 mL/s with a voided volume of 210 mL
Bladder ultrasound for post-void residual: 160 mL
Office flexible cystoscopy: single large bladder stone, trabeculated bladder, obstructing enlarged prostate with a median lobe, no bladder tumor
Transurethral laser cystolitholapaxy; stone analysis 100 percent uric acid
Transurethral resection of the prostate at the same operation; pathology benign prostatic hyperplasia
Arthrocentesis of the left knee: 25 mL of cloudy yellow fluid; needle-shaped, negatively birefringent crystals; Gram stain negative; culture later showed no growth

tr.td: Primary care visit for recurrent gout flares and painful, interrupted urination with blood in the urine
Four-week gout and blood pressure review, with urology consultation for a bladder stone
Review four weeks after stone removal and prostate resection, with urate titration and stone metabolic evaluation
Gout, stone prevention, kidney, and blood pressure review at about six months
Same-day sick visit for a hot, swollen left knee

Start allopurinol 100 mg daily and raise it by 100 mg every 2 to 5 weeks until serum urate is below 6 mg/dL; HLA-B*58:01 testing is not indicated, because he is not of Southeast Asian or African ancestry
Colchicine 0.6 mg daily for three to six months as flare prophylaxis; treat flares with a short prednisone course or extra colchicine, and avoid NSAIDs because of chronic kidney disease
Replace hydrochlorothiazide with losartan, which lowers blood pressure and slightly lowers urate; check potassium and creatinine 2 to 4 weeks after starting
Urology referral to confirm and remove the bladder stone, look for bladder outlet obstruction and other causes of hematuria, and advise on stone prevention
Uric acid stone prevention: fluids for a urine output of at least 2.5 L a day, potassium citrate to a urine pH of 6.0 to 6.5, stone analysis, and a 24-hour urine collection

CMID kidney and blood pressure monitoring: blood pressure every visit; eGFR and urine albumin yearly at G3a A1; calcium, phosphate, and PTH at baseline; hemoglobin and the kidney failure risk equation yearly; statin for age over 50 with eGFR below 60; medication review for NSAIDs every visit
Limit alcohol, especially beer and spirits, and purine-rich meat, organ meat, and shellfish; avoid sugar-sweetened drinks; aim for gradual weight loss and daily walking
Serum urate below 6 mg/dL on allopurinol by the six-month review
Serum urate 5.4 mg/dL on allopurinol 300 mg
Bladder stone removed and comfortable voiding with a normal post-void residual
Stone removed; IPSS from 16 to 6; residual 35 mL
No gout flare for six months after starting urate-lowering therapy
Not met: one knee flare in July while urate was still above target; none since
Urine output of at least 2.5 L a day and urine pH of 6.0 to 6.5
Urine pH 6.3 on potassium citrate; home measuring jug shows about 2.3 L a day
